true_root_cause: Viewers watching the live national-team soccer match reduce app traffic; the -26% drop matches the match's expected -25% impact on impressions, so there is no system fault.

Synthetic alert: the -62% drop is far beyond the match impact, but no ads workload or ad_impressions metric exists in the workshop account, so the evidence cannot confirm a cause or an owning team. The correct outcome is INCONCLUSIVE with a request for ads-side telemetry, not a guessed owner.

order-api POST /orders allocates about 1MB per request into a module-level cache that is never evicted (unbounded cache memory leak), so task memory grows with order volume until tasks hit the memory limit and are OOM-killed. The leaky revision is live because the post-deploy load test that detects it runs after deployment and ECS circuit-breaker rollback is disabled. Whether an OOM kill has already happened depends on how long the environment has been running.
